notes.title: Start here: reading NetSlack with trace tables
notes.body:
NetSlack is a small Slack-style app: an ASP.NET Core minimal API on .NET 8, EF Core over SQLite, SignalR for live messages and a React client. This pack uses four guides from **docs/upskill/**:

1. **04-code-reading-gym/02-trace-tables.md**: five traces (posting a message, a persistence query, the auth boundary, the error contract, a SignalR connect) as tables of file, value shape, owner and risk.
2. **03-architecture-and-patterns/02-data-model-and-persistence.md**: entities, EF Core mappings and transactions.
3. **02-stack-and-language-mastery/01-dotnet-runtime-model.md**: startup, tracking, async and lifetimes.
4. **02-stack-and-language-mastery/03-type-system-and-contracts.md**: nullable types, records, LINQ and exceptions.

Start with the trace tables. For each row, open the cited lines and say in one sentence what the value looks like when it arrives and when it leaves. Most questions in this pack are answered by reading one or two methods carefully: MessageService, ExceptionHandlingMiddleware, CurrentUser and ServiceCollectionExtensions.

notes.title: Core idea: tracked loads, untracked reads and foreign keys
notes.body:
EF Core can load an entity in two modes. A **tracked** load registers the entity with the DbContext's change tracker, which compares it at SaveChanges time and writes any differences, including new items added to its collections. An **untracked** load (AsNoTracking) returns plain objects the context forgets about.

Open MessageService and compare its two private access-check methods line by line. Note which one tracks the channel it loads, and then read what the posting path does with that channel before it saves. Ask yourself why the two methods differ.

Then read GetRecentAsync slowly: write down what each LINQ operator does to the sequence, in order, including both sorts and the value passed to Take.

Last, open MessageConfiguration and ChannelConfiguration. For each foreign key note its OnDelete behavior, and for each index note exactly which columns it covers and whether it is unique. Look up the difference between Cascade, Restrict and SetNull in the EF Core docs.

excerpts.quote: Explain why `AsNoTracking` is appropriate for message reads but not for updating a channel membership.

notes.title: Core idea: from bearer token to user id to status code
notes.body:
Authentication and error handling each have a single owner in NetSlack.

**Tokens.** ServiceCollectionExtensions configures JwtBearer. List every TokenValidationParameters property it sets and look up the default of each one in the Microsoft docs, so you know which defaults this repo changes. Then read the OnMessageReceived event: work out for which requests it reads a token from somewhere other than the Authorization header, and why browsers need that for WebSockets.

**Identity.** CurrentUser turns claims into ICurrentUser. Read how UserId is parsed and exactly what IsAuthenticated requires. Then find where MessageService checks IsAuthenticated and what it throws.

**Errors.** ExceptionHandlingMiddleware maps exception types to statuses with a switch expression. Build a table with one row per arm: exception type, status, and the text that reaches the client as Title and Detail. Look up what ArgumentException.Message returns when it is constructed with a parameter name.

notes.title: Core idea: nullable types, build settings and JSON shapes
notes.body:
C# nullable reference types let the compiler warn when a non-nullable reference might be null, for example a string property that a constructor never assigns. Those are warnings by default. Open **Directory.Build.props** at the repo root: it applies its settings to every project. Read each property and look up what it changes for the whole build.

Next, look at the private parameterless constructors in UserProfile, Workspace and Channel. EF Core uses such constructors to create objects when it reads rows. Ask what those constructors assign and why they need to.

Finally, follow ChannelType from the C# enum to the TypeScript union in client/src/api/types.ts. Look up how System.Text.Json writes an enum by default, then search Program.cs for every place that changes that, and note which serializer each change applies to (minimal API responses and the SignalR hub use separate settings).

excerpts.quote: **Concept:** Nullable reference types make null a visible design choice.

notes.title: Clamp to 100, take the newest, then sort ascending
notes.body:
**Key: the newest 100 messages, listed from oldest to newest.**

GetRecentAsync computes `Math.Clamp(take, 1, 100)`, so 500 becomes 100. The query then orders by PostedAt descending and takes 100, which selects the newest 100, and finally re-orders by PostedAt ascending, so the list reads oldest to newest like a chat window.

Why the others are wrong:
- **All 500**: the clamp runs before the value reaches Take.
- **A 400 error**: nothing validates take; out-of-range values are silently bounded.
- **The oldest 100**: the first sort is descending, so Take keeps the most recent rows.

notes.title: Posting to a public channel joins you to it
notes.body:
**Key: the post succeeds, and they are saved as a channel member too.**

EnsureCanPostChannelAsync first requires workspace membership. For a public channel it then calls channel.Join(currentUser.UserId) and returns. The channel was loaded with tracking, so the new ChannelMember is detected and inserted by the same SaveChangesAsync that inserts the message.

Why the others are wrong:
- **A 403 for non-members**: that check (line 109) runs only for channels that are not public.
- **Member list unchanged**: Join adds to the tracked aggregate, and the save persists it.
- **A 404**: NotFoundException is thrown only when no channel has that id.

notes.title: Not a member of a private channel: 403
notes.body:
**Key: 403, with the detail "You do not have access to this channel."**

EnsureCanReadChannelAsync loads the channel and checks two things: workspace membership, and, for a non-public channel, channel membership. A workspace member outside a private channel fails the second check, so it throws ForbiddenException with that message. The middleware maps ForbiddenException to 403 and copies the message into Title and Detail.

Why the others are wrong:
- **404 to hide it**: 404 is thrown only when the channel id does not exist.
- **200 with an empty list**: the check throws before any message query runs.
- **401**: the token is valid; channel access is not a claim.

excerpts.quote: throw new ForbiddenException("You do not have access to this channel.");

notes.title: ArgumentException.Message includes the parameter name
notes.body:
**Key: body is required. (Parameter 'body')**

Guard.AgainstEmpty throws `new ArgumentException($"{parameterName} is required.", parameterName)`. ExceptionHandlingMiddleware maps ArgumentException to 400 and sets Title (and Detail) to exception.Message. On .NET Core 3.0 and later, when an ArgumentException has a ParamName, its Message property appends " (Parameter 'body')" to the text you passed.

Why the others are wrong:
- **The body field is required.**: that wording is ASP.NET model validation, which this code path never uses.
- **Unexpected server error.**: that title is used only for exceptions that fall through to 500.
- **One or more validation errors occurred.**: the default ValidationProblemDetails title; no validation problem is produced here.

excerpts.quote: throw new ArgumentException($"{parameterName} is required.", parameterName);

notes.title: Unmapped exceptions become a generic, logged 500
notes.body:
**Key: a 500 with a generic title and detail; the real error is only logged.**

The switch maps NotFound, Forbidden, Conflict and ArgumentException; DbUpdateException matches none, so status is 500. For a 500 the middleware calls logger.LogError with the exception and writes fixed text: "Unexpected server error." and "The request failed unexpectedly.". A traceId is added so the log entry can be found.

Why the others are wrong:
- **Detail carries the message**: the message is used only for the mapped, non-500 statuses.
- **409 for database failures**: only ConflictException maps to 409.
- **400 via ArgumentException**: DbUpdateException derives from Exception, not from ArgumentException.

notes.title: This repo cuts the clock skew to one minute
notes.body:
**Key: it is rejected, because ClockSkew is set to one minute here.**

TokenValidationParameters.ClockSkew defaults to five minutes, but ServiceCollectionExtensions sets `ClockSkew = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1)` alongside ValidateLifetime = true. A token 90 seconds past exp is outside that window, so JwtBearer fails it and the protected endpoint answers 401.

Why the others are wrong:
- **Accepted, five minutes of skew**: that is the framework default, which this code overrides.
- **ValidateLifetime is false**: it is set to true on line 38.
- **Only if the key changed**: expiry is checked independently of the signature.

notes.title: Query-string tokens are accepted only for the hub
notes.body:
**Key: 401: the query token is read only for paths under /hubs/messages.**

JwtBearer reads the Authorization header by default and never looks at the query string. The OnMessageReceived event adds one exception: if access_token is present and the path StartsWithSegments("/hubs/messages"), it sets context.Token. Browsers cannot send headers on a WebSocket upgrade, which is why the hub needs this. A REST path does not match, so no token is found and RequireAuthorization returns 401.

Why the others are wrong:
- **JwtBearer reads ?access_token everywhere**: it does not by default.
- **Any query token is copied**: the path condition prevents that.
- **403 with no roles**: the request is never authenticated, so it is 401.

notes.title: A valid token without a user id gets 403 here
notes.body:
**Key: 403, because CurrentUser reports an empty id as not authenticated.**

JwtBearer does not require a subject claim; it validates signature, issuer, audience and lifetime, so the principal is authenticated and RequireAuthorization lets the request in. CurrentUser.UserId uses Guid.TryParse and returns Guid.Empty when the claim is missing, and IsAuthenticated is true only when the identity is authenticated AND UserId != Guid.Empty. MessageService sees false and throws ForbiddenException, which maps to 403. The trace table calls this "unauthenticated", but the status code is 403.

Why the others are wrong:
- **401 from JwtBearer**: no sub requirement exists in the validation parameters.
- **200 as Guid.Empty**: the access check throws first.
- **500 from Guid.Parse**: the code uses TryParse.

excerpts.quote: public bool IsAuthenticated => httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.User.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true && UserId != Guid.Empty;

notes.title: Restrict keeps authors with messages from being deleted
notes.body:
**Key: the delete fails: Restrict blocks removing an author who has messages.**

MessageConfiguration declares the author relationship with OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict). EF will not cascade or null out the dependents: if messages are tracked it throws before saving, and otherwise the database foreign key rejects the DELETE. Either way the profile stays.

Why the others are wrong:
- **Messages deleted too**: that is Cascade, which this file uses for the channel relationship, not the author one.
- **AuthorId set to null**: that is SetNull, and AuthorId is a non-nullable Guid.
- **Dangling AuthorId**: the foreign key exists precisely to prevent that.

notes.title: Channel names are unique per workspace
notes.body:
**Key: both, since the unique index covers WorkspaceId and Name together.**

ChannelConfiguration declares one composite unique index over (WorkspaceId, Name). Uniqueness applies to the pair, so general can exist once in each workspace, while a second general in the same workspace violates the index.

Why the others are wrong:
- **Unique across the database**: that would need an index on Name alone.
- **No index at all**: line 19 declares one.
- **Only if one is private**: Type is not part of the index, so it changes nothing.

notes.title: Two serializers, two string-enum converters
notes.body:
**Key: as its name, such as "Public", on both paths.**

System.Text.Json writes enums as numbers by default. Program.cs adds a JsonStringEnumConverter to ConfigureHttpJsonOptions, which minimal API results use, and another to AddJsonProtocol's PayloadSerializerOptions, which SignalR uses. With both registered, every ChannelType leaves the server as its name.

Why the others are wrong:
- **Number over HTTP**: the HTTP options have the converter.
- **Number on both by default**: the default is overridden on both paths.
- **Lowercase "public"**: the converter is created without a naming policy, so it keeps the C# member name.

notes.title: Nullable warnings are build errors in this repo
notes.body:
**Key: the build fails, since TreatWarningsAsErrors makes CS8618 an error.**

Directory.Build.props sets Nullable to enable and TreatWarningsAsErrors to true for every project. DisplayName, Email and AvatarUrl are non-nullable strings, so a constructor that exits without assigning them triggers CS8618. Normally that is a warning; here it is an error and the build stops.

Why the others are wrong:
- **EF throws at startup**: EF sets mapped properties itself after construction; it does not need initial values.
- **Only public constructors are checked**: nullable analysis covers every constructor, private ones included.
- **Builds, then loads nulls**: it never builds, and EF fills the required columns when it materializes a row.

notes.title: The post path changes the channel, so it must be tracked
notes.body:
**Key: Join adds a member to the channel, which the later save must persist.**

The read path only checks access, so AsNoTracking is enough. The post path may call channel.Join for a public channel, which adds a ChannelMember to the loaded aggregate. SaveChangesAsync finds that new member only because the channel is tracked; with AsNoTracking the join would be lost silently.

Why the others are wrong:
- **Include returns no rows untracked**: Include loads related rows in both modes.
- **Skipping the unique index**: tracking has nothing to do with index use.
- **A row lock until save**: EF takes no lock when it reads; tracking is in-memory bookkeeping.
